item.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery for a SaaS publisher
item.description:
Scope of the study

Fictional organisation: Brumaille Logiciels. Publisher of an online booking application (SaaS) for local shops, about 40 people (14 in development, 6 in operations and security, 8 in support and customer success, 12 in sales, finance and management). The application is hosted with a cloud provider (not named), in a single region, and clients pay a monthly subscription.

Goal: show how to build a business continuity and disaster recovery plan end to end: business impact analysis (BIA), scenarios, strategies, recovery plan, tests and indicators. The approach draws on the principles of ISO 22301 (business continuity management) and, on the IT side, ISO/IEC 27031 (ICT readiness for business continuity). Measures are linked to ISO/IEC 27002:2022.

item.title: GDPR compliance of a health centre
item.description:
Scope of the study

Fictional organisation: Les Alisiers health centre. A neighbourhood health centre of about 30 people (6 doctors, 12 nurses and allied health staff, 6 medical secretaries and reception staff, 4 administration and management staff, 2 for logistics and technical work), following about 6,000 active patients (assumption). The name, headcount and figures are invented.

Goal: show the approach of a first compliance exercise under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR): map the processing activities, check legal bases and retention periods, frame processors, organise data subject rights, carry out an impact assessment on one high-risk processing, link security to ISO/IEC 27002:2022 and know how to react to a personal data breach.

item.title: Incident response: compromised admin account and ransomware
item.description:
Scope of the study

Fictional organisation: Fictilog. A logistics and warehousing SME of about 60 people on two sites: a head office (offices and main warehouse) and a secondary site (“site B”: warehouse and loading dock). It manages stock for industrial clients and employs drivers and order pickers.

Goal: show how an incident response unfolds, from detection to lessons learned, with reasoned decisions and their consequences. The study follows the NIST incident response lifecycle (SP 800-61, whose revision 2 describes four phases) and ISO/IEC 27035, and links each step to the ISO/IEC 27002:2022 controls.

item.title: ISO 27005 risk analysis of an accounting firm
item.description:
Scope of the study

Fictional organisation: Aubépine firm. A 14-person accounting firm (2 partners, 9 accountants, 3 assistants) that keeps the books and payroll of about 180 clients, mostly very small businesses.

Goal: show a risk analysis from start to finish, following the ISO/IEC 27005 approach (information security risk management) and linked to the ISO/IEC 27002:2022 controls. It is the first building block of an ISO 27001 ISMS, but the study stops at the analysis and the treatment plan.
